ideaBrief.title: Void Office Tycoon
ideaBrief.coreMetaphor: A small office grows inside an empty void.
ideaBrief.successVision: Students learn project management by building departments and escaping the void.

proposalState.deliverableArea: Simple web tycoon game for learning IT project management
proposalState.problemStatement: In COM0463, some students know project terms but do not see how they connect. Scope, budget, team work, and quality can feel separate. This game makes them visible as office parts inside a void and targets about 15% better post-quiz results.
proposalState.targetPopulation: Around 40 COM0463 IT Project Management students.
successCriteria: At least 75% of students explain one good department choice.
At least 30 students play one full office run.
Each student finishes one minigame and buys one department.

userStories.soThat: I can earn points for my office.
userStories.acc: Given a minigame starts, When I finish it, Then I receive main points and one resource result.

userStories.soThat: my office can grow in the void.
userStories.acc: Given I have enough points, When I buy a department, Then it appears on the office map.

userStories.want: to choose between Budget, Team, and Quality upgrades
userStories.soThat: I can plan my project strategy.
userStories.acc: Given I choose a department, When it is built, Then one resource increases more than the others.

userStories.want: to see the final office report
userStories.soThat: I can discuss student decisions in class.
userStories.acc: Given the game is finished, When I open the report, Then I can see departments, resources, and key choices.

userStories.want: to pause the game for explanation
userStories.soThat: confused students can follow the activity.
userStories.acc: Given students are confused, When I pause the session, Then the current office state stays visible.

frs.description: System shall show a void office map with locked and built departments.
System shall run short timed minigames and give points.
System shall keep a simple log with studentId, minigameId, departmentBuilt, resourceChange, timestamp, and final result.

nfrs.desc: The game should not feel slow.
Students should understand the office screen easily.
Student data should not be shared publicly.
nfrs.target: Use simple class IDs instead of public names

nfrs.desc: Text, timers, and buttons should be easy to read.
The game should keep progress during the class.

proposalState.logPrivacy: The game keeps a simple log of choices, scores, and built departments. The log is only for class feedback.
proposalState.dataCollectionPlan: I will use quiz results, game logs, and a short reflection about the final office.

bloomOutcomes.outcome: Remember basic project terms like scope, budget, team, and quality.
Explain why Budget, Team, and Quality matter in a project.
Use points to buy a useful department in the office.
Compare two department choices and explain the better one.
Judge if the office plan was balanced enough to escape.
Create a short improved office expansion plan.

mdaAnalysis.mechanics: Timed minigames, main points, Budget, Team, Quality, and department unlocks.
mdaAnalysis.dynamics: Students balance quick minigame results with slower office planning.
mdaAnalysis.aesthetics: The game should feel like a strange office slowly appearing in empty space.

proposalState.sdtAutonomy: Students choose which department to build and which resource to improve.
proposalState.sdtCompetence: Students get quick feedback after each minigame, so they can improve the next office choice.
proposalState.sdtRelatedness: Students compare office layouts and explain why their department order worked or failed.
proposalState.narrativeTheme: The player starts with one desk floating in a dark void. Fast project minigames create main points, Budget, Team, and Quality. Departments like Scope Desk, Bug Lab, Sprint Floor, Risk Vault, and Stakeholder Booth appear when the player spends points. The final Portal Room opens when the office is strong enough. Self-Determination Theory is used because students choose upgrades. Mechanics-Dynamics-Aesthetics connects minigames with the feeling of building the office. Bloom Taxonomy moves students from terms to planning. Kirkpatrick four-level evaluation is used with reaction, quiz, transfer, and result checks.
proposalState.gameOverview: The player builds an IT project office inside a void. Each round has a short arcade-style project minigame. Points buy departments. Budget, Team, and Quality change based on the player's department choices. When enough departments are built, the Portal Room opens and the office escapes.

scenarios.title: Scope Fog
scenarios.setup: Requirement notes float across the void and the timer starts.
scenarios.winCondition: The student sorts must-have and nice-to-have items correctly.
scenarios.loseCondition: If items are mixed badly, losePoints=0 and office growth slows for debrief.
scenarios.outcome: Students see why scope control protects Budget and Team.

scenarios.title: Bug Rain
scenarios.setup: Bugs fall onto the office floor during a release sprint.
scenarios.winCondition: The student catches serious bugs before minor bugs.
scenarios.loseCondition: If serious bugs are missed, losePoints=0 and Quality drops for discussion.
scenarios.outcome: Students see why testing and quality choices matter.

scenarios.title: Budget Rift
scenarios.setup: A rift opens and offers three department upgrades with different costs.
scenarios.winCondition: The student chooses an upgrade that keeps Budget, Team, and Quality balanced.
scenarios.loseCondition: If one resource becomes too weak, losePoints=0 and the class reviews the choice.
scenarios.outcome: Students see how project trade-offs affect the final goal.

proposalState.gameDuration: About 60 to 75 minutes including explanation, play, and debrief.

sessionSteps.name: Introduction
sessionSteps.description: Instructor explains the office goal, resources, and minigames.

sessionSteps.name: Play
sessionSteps.description: Students play minigames and build departments.

sessionSteps.name: Debrief
sessionSteps.description: Class discusses office choices and project trade-offs.

sessionSteps.name: Report
sessionSteps.description: Students write a short improved office expansion plan.

gamePhases.name: Earn
gamePhases.description: Receive main points and resource changes.

gamePhases.name: Build
gamePhases.description: Buy or upgrade one office department.

gamePhases.name: Escape Check
gamePhases.description: Check if the Portal Room can open.

rewardStructure.elite: Students who open the Portal Room get an Escape Architect badge.
rewardStructure.professional: Students who build three departments get a Department Builder badge.
rewardStructure.access: All students get the final office report and debrief notes.

kpis.target: More balanced scope, resource, and quality notes
Better planning section than the first draft

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Make timers adjustable for the class.
tuslerRisks.preventive: Test minigame speed before the lesson.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Slow the timer and give one example round.

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Use clear labels for points and resources.
tuslerRisks.preventive: Show the resource meanings before play.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Explain Budget, Team, and Quality again during pause.

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Prepare a backup activity if the game does not load.
tuslerRisks.preventive: Test the browser and projector before class.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Use paper department cards and discuss choices.

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Collect small spelling and balance issues after the session.
tuslerRisks.preventive: Do a quick peer review before submission.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Fix small issues in the next version.

proposalState.facilitatorRole: The facilitator explains the rules, helps confused students, pauses if needed, and leads the final discussion.
proposalState.wf_dash: The dashboard shows the void office map, main points, Budget, Team, Quality, the current minigame, and the next department price.
proposalState.wf_asset: Each department tile shows its name, price, resource effect, locked or built state, and a short project management meaning.
proposalState.wf_portfolio: The report page shows built departments, resource levels, minigame results, the escape result, and a short reflection.
proposalState.inScope: The project includes a void office map, fast minigames, main points, Budget, Team, Quality, department buying, and losePoints=0 for failed cases.
proposalState.outScope: The project does not include real company data, VR, real money, online multiplayer, or advanced simulation.
proposalState.whyMotivation: Students may care more when their project choices make the office grow and move them closer to escaping the void.
proposalState.howEthics: The game should use simple student IDs and avoid public ranking by real names.

tuslerRisks.responsive: Use paper department cards and discuss choices.

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Collect small spelling and balance issues after the session.
tuslerRisks.preventive: Do a quick peer review before submission.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Fix small issues in the next version.

state.facilitatorRole: The facilitator explains the rules, helps confused students, pauses if needed, and leads the final discussion.
state.wf_dash: The dashboard shows the void office map, main points, Budget, Team, Quality, the current minigame, and the next department price.
state.wf_asset: Each department tile shows its name, price, resource effect, locked or built state, and a short project management meaning.
state.wf_portfolio: The report page shows built departments, resource levels, minigame results, the escape result, and a short reflection.
state.inScope: The project includes a void office map, fast minigames, main points, Budget, Team, Quality, department buying, and losePoints=0 for failed cases.
state.outScope: The project does not include real company data, VR, real money, online multiplayer, or advanced simulation.
state.whyMotivation: Students may care more when their project choices make the office grow and move them closer to escaping the void.
state.howEthics: The game should use simple student IDs and avoid public ranking by real names.
